summary:
The Falkland Islands are a British Overseas Territory with their own Legislative Assembly, which legislates locally. Same-sex activity has been legal since 1989 and the age of consent has been equal since 2005.

Same-sex marriage and civil partnerships have been available since 29 April 2017. The Legislative Assembly passed the bill in March 2017 by 7 votes to 1, and the registrar general confirmed by reply in June 2017 that it is law. Civil partnerships are open to opposite-sex couples as well as same-sex couples. A public consultation ahead of the bill showed 90% support for same-sex marriage and 94% for civil partnerships in a territory of roughly 3,000 residents.

The Constitution Order 2008, at Article 16, bans discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation. The provision covers sexual orientation only; the sources do not identify a gender-identity ground in the Constitution.

United Kingdom frameworks do not reach the Islands. The UK Equality Act 2010 and the Gender Recognition Act 2004 do not extend to the Falkland Islands, so protection and recognition depend on the territory's own ordinances.

Legal gender change has been possible since 2014. There is no self-identification route and no recognition of non-binary status, and holders of a UK Gender Recognition Certificate are recognised in their acquired gender under the CPE Ordinance 2014.

Three ordinances frame the criminal-justice treatment of bias. The Crimes Ordinance 2014 provides for hate-stirring on grounds of sexual orientation, the CPE Ordinance 2014 provides for sexual orientation as an aggravating factor in sentencing, and a Prisons Ordinance was enacted in 2017.

Stepchild and joint adoption have been available to same-sex couples since 2017.

The United Kingdom is responsible for the territory's defence.
tangentialFactors:
The registrar general's June 2017 reply also confirmed that same-sex marriage is not legal in the South Georgia and South Sandwich Islands dependency, so the equality reform does not extend to that neighbouring British territory.

Public attitudes in the territory are reported as largely positive, consistent with the 90% consultation support for same-sex marriage.

outOfScopeNotes:
The sources identify sexual orientation as the only protected ground in the Constitution Order 2008; whether any gender-identity protection exists under other Falkland Islands instruments is unresolved in this inventory.

Enforcement practice under the Crimes Ordinance 2014 hate-stirring provision and the CPE Ordinance 2014 sentencing aggravation is not sourced here, so their application in reported cases remains unresolved.

The Prisons Ordinance 2017 is identified by date only; its specific provisions on trans detainees are not sourced in this inventory.
